Claims of American citizens against Panama growing out of riots in 1915. Reports acquittal of Nunez.

Same subject. Instructs him in sense of War Department’s Mar. 27.
Railway and road construction jointly by the United States and Panama. Commission appointed to go to the United States for negotiation.
Concession to B. B. Duncan. Incloses copy of letter from Mr. Duncan giving assurance that it is his aim to work in harmony with Government of the United States.
Railway and road construction jointly by the United States and Panama. Announces arrival of special mission and asks an audience.

Concession to B. B. Duncan. Incloses note from Foreign Office by which it is agreed that the Executive Power will consult American Government before authorizing branch lines.

Railway and road construction jointly by the United States and Panama. Outlines program of road construction as approved by the War Department.

Concession to B. B. Duncan. Acknowledges receipt of Legation’s 1430 of June 16.

Railway and road construction jointly by the United States and Panama. Legation’s note of the 27th is receiving consideration.

Railway and road construction jointly by the United States and Panama. Incloses copy of War Department’s Aug. 17.
Claims of American citizens against Panama growing out of riots in 1915. Incloses reply of Foreign Office to presentation of claims.

Political affairs. Revolution started; loyal troops joined popular movement; former officials murdered; provisional government set up by 12 members of Duma and social democrats; movement general throughout Empire; Emperor abdicated in favor brother.

Same subject. Quotes statement abdication of Emperor and son in favor former’s brother who replied will accept if people wish; Milioukoff recognized by Foreign Office; workingmen’s committee demand republic; quiet prevails.
Same subject. Transmits copy of communication from Minister of Foreign Affairs outlining in detail the events of the revolution.

Same subject. Reports no opposition to Provisional Government and requests authority to recognize it, as first recognition by the United States is desirable from every viewpoint; life of Government depends upon its ability to prosecute the war.
Same subject. Refers his Mar. 18 and instructs him inform Milioukov this Government recognizes the provisional one.
Same subject. Reports fully on conditions in Petrograd and details leading up to the revolution.
Same subject. Quotes his speech made before Council of Ministers formally recognizing Provisional Government; other countries follow.
Same subject. Incloses note from Foreign Office thanking the American Government for recognition of the Provisional Government.
President’s message. Incloses translation of that portion of President’s message to the National Assembly which refers to Salvador’s relations with the United States.
Earthquake. Volcano of San Salvador erupts, seven quakes one evening, Legation uninhabitable but records safe; no deaths.
Same subject. Convey sympathy of the United States and offer assistance.
Same subject. Extends sympathy and offers aid and assistance.
Same subject. If necessary Red Cross can cable money; cable Department what articles food and clothing needed and suggest method of transportation from the United States.
Same subject. Acknowledges with thanks the expression of sympathy extended to his people.
Same subject. President Melendez appreciates offer of assistance but thinks Salvador can deal with situation.
Same subject. Quakes continue, many homes leveled to ground; many leaving city.
Same subject. Quotes Long’s telegram reporting quake; hardly house left in capital for use as living quarters; requests instructions.
Same subject. Preparations being made to cope with situation; reports articles needed from American Government.
Same subject. Heavy demands made upon Salvadorean Government; makes suggestions as to method of help.
Same subject. Contents of his June 11 sent to Red Cross which will render all aid possible.
Same subject. Red Cross has placed money to his credit with Bloom Bros.; question of further supplies being taken up.
Same subject. Commission appointed to receive relief funds; asks $10,000 be provided immediately, also that benevolent fund of $5,000 and supplies listed in his June 11 be placed at his discretion.
Same subject. Thousands sleep in the open in heavy rain; three quakes during night.
Same subject. Salvadorean Red Cross accepts money, supplementary fund necessary.
Same subject. Makes report on earthquake; conditions improving.
Same subject. Funds not adequate to make permanent repairs; suggests a loan be offered.
Same subject. Red Cross states that in addition to money deposited with Bloom Bros., it is sniping supplies requested by him in his June 11 on June 25.
Same subject. Little progress made in rehabilitating the city account lack of funds; general outline of conditions.
Same subject. Supplementary fund alone will make possible effective use of supplies; mentions further list of articles needed.
